decision.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Economic growth slowed in the first part of this year and the adjustment in the housing sector is ongoing.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its view on the economy to note that growth slowed in the first part of this year.

changes.quote: Nevertheless, the economy seems likely to expand at a moderate pace over coming quarters.
changes.explanation: The Fed trimmed the word continue from its growth outlook.
The Fed adjusted its assessment to state that core inflation remains somewhat elevated.

tone_quotes.quote: In these circumstances, the Committee's predominant policy concern remains the risk that inflation will fail to moderate as expected.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.41% APR costs about $55.88 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.67% and moved +4 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.16% would rise by about $7.78 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.5%, and employers added an average of 125k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.6% over the past year (April 2007); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +5 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.08% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future policy adjustments will depend on incoming information regarding inflation and economic growth. An educational forecast model gives the next meeting a hold probability of 62 percent.
